objective: Stop expired sign-in material accumulating without bound. POST /api/auth/passkey/options is on the unauthenticated allowlist (server/routes/guard.ts ~102) and inserts a webauthn_challenges row per call (server/repos/passkeys.ts ~298), and `forgetExpiredChallenges` (passkeys.ts ~324) has no caller — so an anonymous caller can grow that table indefinitely. `purgeExpiredSessions` (server/repos/identity.ts ~748) has no caller either, so expired session digests pile up. Add server/services/housekeeping.ts with `sweepExpiredCredentials(now)` and call it from the fleet-wide part of the durable Russell tick in server/services/russell/loop.ts, rate-limited to at most once per interval and wrapped so a failure is logged and never stops the rest of the tick.
expectedOutcome: sweepExpiredCredentials deletes webauthn challenges past their expiry (via forgetExpiredChallenges) and sessions whose expiry is older than a named grace constant (via purgeExpiredSessions(before), passing now minus the grace period), and returns the two counts. Live challenges, unexpired sessions and sessions expired within the grace period survive. loop.ts calls it at most once per HOUSEKEEPING_INTERVAL_MS, inside a try/catch that logs and continues.
nonGoals: Any edit under server/services/identity/** or to authentication or session semantics.
Deleting audit rows (identity_events), OAuth tokens, invitations or anything append-only.
A migration or a new scheduler: it rides the existing durable tick.

acceptanceConditions.statement: An expired challenge is deleted and an unexpired one survives.
A session expired beyond the grace period is deleted; an unexpired session and one expired within the grace period survive.
A sweep that throws (injected) is caught and the rest of the tick still runs.
A second call inside the interval performs no deletes; a test reading server/services/russell/loop.ts asserts the sweep is reached from the tick.

rollbackRequirement: Discard the branch. Deletes only rows that are already expired and inert; no schema or policy change.
